skills.name: Practical preparation: credit-creation records in Cameroon

note.text: Use fictional banks and invented CFA-franc amounts, not actual account details. Prepare columns for incoming deposit, stipulated retained fraction and next redeposit. Calculate each round from its predecessor. Compare a finite sum with the limiting model total. Record which assumptions permit the chain. A local currency or place name does not turn a hypothetical fraction into a Cameroon regulation or make the result an observed banking statistic.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to construct a finite deposit-round record and identify why it is not an observed lending total. Builds on: loan/deposit entries and the stylised multiplier. Leads to: BEAC, central-bank functions and evidence-based interpretation.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Original model banks A, B and C: deposit {10000}, retained fraction {20}/{100}. Subsequent deposits are {10000*(1-20/100)} and {10000*(1-20/100)*(1-20/100)}. The finite sum is {10000+10000*(1-20/100)+10000*(1-20/100)*(1-20/100)}; the limiting model total is {10000/(20/100)}. No real customers, banks or current reserve ratios are represented.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Write assumptions above the table. Multiply by the fraction left after retention to find the next deposit. Add exactly the rounds requested. Explain how incomplete redepositing or a decision not to lend would change the assumed sequence; actual lending requires separate evidence.

questions.prompt: Invented Cameroon classroom model: an initial deposit is {D} CFA francs and each bank retains {r}% of its received deposit. Each remaining amount is fully lent and redeposited at the next bank. Add only the initial deposit and the next two deposits; do not use the infinite total.

misconceptions.explain: That includes all indefinitely assumed rounds, not just the stated initial and next two deposits.
That omits the initial deposit the question expressly includes.

solution: Initial deposit: {D}. Next deposit: {D*(1-r/100)}. Following deposit: {D*(1-r/100)*(1-r/100)}.
This finite sum is below the stipulated limiting total {D*100/r}.
